OMP-431-s03 pinned egress fetch and push, using the s01 address and destination rules. Resolver(host, port) returns addresses; Connector(ip, port, timeout) returns a socket. open_pinned resolves at call time with no cache: a blocked IP literal raises EgressRefused with the blocked_address code and calls neither the resolver nor the connector; an empty answer is invalid; any blocked answer raises EgressRefused with that code and the offending ip and does not connect; a public IP literal must resolve only to itself or the answer is invalid; otherwise the connector is called with the first address, that port, and the timeout (default 30s). tls wraps the socket with the default SSL context (CERT_REQUIRED, check_hostname, optional ca_bundle) and SNI equal to the host. ResearchFetchService.fetch records every call on channel fetch with the request url and the identity mission, worker, workspace, project, and stage. A non-http(s) URL is scheme_not_allowed and a missing host is invalid, both before any lookup or send. A research_refusal hit raises EgressRefused with that s01 code (method_not_allowed, request_body, auth_header, url_credentials, query_credential) and sends nothing. A clean http(s) GET or HEAD is vetted, then open_pinned looks the name up again and connects to the connect-time address; the vet lookup is not reused, so a public address at vet and a blocked address at connect is refused and the connector is not called. One request is issued with the caller headers only (no Authorization, Cookie, or Proxy-Authorization is added), redirects are not followed, and no cookie jar is kept. Set-Cookie and Set-Cookie2 are dropped. Statuses such as 302 and 401 are returned as FetchResult(status, headers, body). A certificate failure is recorded as tls_error and re-raised; another exchange failure is recorded as exchange_failed. check_push_destination requires https (else scheme_not_allowed), a host, no userinfo (else url_credentials), and no blocked IP literal (else the blocked_address code). The origin must be granted by an unexpired network_access destination under the s01 rule: exact scheme, normalized host, and port; accepted forms are https://h[:p], http://h[:p], h:p as https, h as https port 443, and bracketed [v6] or [v6]:port; a path other than empty or /, a query, a fragment, userinfo, or another scheme grants nothing; expires_at <= now is expired and a naive expiry is UTC; the caller now is used, not the wall clock; a non-network_access policy does not grant. Otherwise destination_not_allowed. The granting policy id is returned. deliver_push runs that check again, POSTs once through open_pinned with TLS, drops Set-Cookie and Set-Cookie2, and records channel push (klass standing and the policy id when the origin was granted; klass none when the check itself refuses).

OMP-431-s04: asyncio default-deny egress HTTP proxy. One unix socket per sandbox identity at <dir>/proxy.sock (mode 0600), created by open_sandbox(identity, dir) and removed by close_sandbox(identity); the identity is the sandbox binding and is never read from a request (an X-OMP-Mission header is ignored). One request per client connection; the policy is read fresh from policy_source(identity, now) for each request; every client response carries Connection: close and the connection then closes, so pipelined bytes are dropped. Plain absolute-form requests: a refusal is 403 with JSON {"code": code} and one EgressRecord; a research identity is delegated to the s03 fetch service (channel fetch, the service's own record) for both allow and refusal; a model destination is forwarded to model_proxy_upstream; an allowed registry, remote, or standing destination is dialed by resolver(host) and connector(ip, port, timeout) and sent origin-form with Connection: close; the upstream response is relayed and recorded (channel http) with the effective host, port, ip, url, klass, and policy_id. A registry is stored as https and decide never matches it for an http request, so an http absolute-form request whose destination the policy also defines as an https origin is re-judged as that https origin while a genuinely unnamed destination still refuses destination_not_allowed. CONNECT host:port is judged as an https tunnel: model destinations and standing destinations whose host is not a project remote are tunnelled (200 Connection Established) and recorded (channel connect); a standing destination whose host is a project remote is inspected instead of opened as an opaque tunnel, so the inner request is decided (tls unset records klass standing, code tls_inspection_required, and does not dial); registry, remote, and research destinations need TLS inspection and are refused tls_inspection_required when tls is unset; anything else gets decide's code (destination_not_allowed, including an IP literal); with tls set to a GatewayCA the gateway replies 200, upgrades the client connection to a CA-signed leaf for the tunnel authority, reads exactly one inner request, and re-runs the plain-http path for it as https with tunnel False against the tunnel authority (the inner request's own host and scheme are ignored, so a relative or absolute target is judged as https against the authority); a leaf that cannot be minted, an empty inner read, an unverifiable upstream certificate (recorded tls_error), and an upstream dial failure (recorded upstream_failed) all end the request with no inner request reaching the upstream; the same one-request Connection: close rule and the same verdicts apply, the upstream leg is TLS with SNI equal to the host verified against system trust or upstream_ca_bundle, and research still goes to the s03 fetch service as an https URL. Every record names the bound identity's workspace, project, mission, worker, and stage.

OMP-431 egress address policy: blocked_address refuses an egress target with invalid (unparseable), metadata (169.254.169.254, 168.63.129.16, 100.100.100.200, fd00:ec2::254), nat64_u_octet (RFC 6052 64:ff9b:1::/48 with a non-zero u-octet), or not_global (not globally routable, or multicast), and returns None only for a globally routable unicast address; IPv6 transition formats are unwrapped to the embedded IPv4 first: IPv4-mapped, IPv4-compatible ::/96 (except :: and ::1), 6to4 2002::/16, Teredo client, and NAT64 64:ff9b::/96 and 64:ff9b:1::/48; Identity frozen dataclass; research_refusal refusing non-GET/HEAD, request bodies, auth headers, URL credentials, and query credentials; EgressRecord frozen dataclass; EgressRecorder protocol and MemoryRecorder; build_policy (the only EgressPolicy constructor, no worktree input) normalizes a host by lower-casing, dropping a trailing dot, stripping brackets, and canonicalizing an IP literal, requires model_proxy ("host:port" or "[v6]:port", explicit port) or raises ValueError, keeps a registry only as https://host[:port] (default 443; other scheme/path/query/fragment/userinfo dropped), keeps a remote only as an http(s) URL without userinfo/query/fragment and with a non-empty repo path (trailing "/" and one ".git" stripped; a percent-decoded empty/"."/".." segment drops it; ssh:// and scp-like git@host:path dropped), and keeps only network_access standing policies whose expires_at is None or after now (naive = UTC); egress_change_kind classifies an egress transition: None old -> create, subsets of registries and remotes -> narrow, new/changed remote or registry -> widen; OMP-431-s01-s05: Request frozen dataclass (scheme, host, port, method, path, query, headers, has_body, tunnel) and Verdict frozen dataclass (allowed, klass model|registry|remote|standing|research|none, code, policy_id); decide(policy, identity, req, now) normalizes the host, defaults a missing port to 443 (https) or 80 (http), treats tunnel as method CONNECT, and applies in order: (1) (host,port) equal policy.model_proxy -> allowed model; (2) research stage -> refused research with the research_refusal code, else allowed research; (3) a standing destination grants the request's exact scheme, host, and port for any request path or query (forms https://h[:p], http://h[:p], h:p as https, h as https:443, and bracketed [v6] or [v6]:port as https; a destination whose path is not "/" or empty, or that carries a query, fragment, userinfo, or another scheme, grants nothing, as does a policy expired at now; an IP literal matches only itself) -> allowed standing with policy_id=str(policy.policy_id); (4) registry: https and (host,port) in policy.registries -> tunnel or non-GET/HEAD is method_not_allowed, body is request_body, else allowed with policy_id=policy.decision_id; OMP-431-s01-s06: (5) remote (repository stage): matches (scheme, host, port, repo) when scheme, normalized host, and default-filled port match and its repeatedly percent-decoded safe path (empty, ".", ".." segments or backslash drop match) equals repo or lies under it by whole segment with optional ".git" (/o/r, /o/r.git, /o/r/..., /o/r.git/...; not /o/rx); read-only rule in order: query service=git-receive-pack (any case) or path ending /git-receive-pack -> refused remote, git_receive_pack; POST allowed only when path is exactly <repo>/git-upload-pack or <repo>.git/git-upload-pack, otherwise method_not_allowed; tunnel or method other than GET/HEAD -> method_not_allowed; GET/HEAD with body -> request_body; else allowed remote with policy_id=policy.decision_id; (6) otherwise refused, klass none, destination_not_allowed; a refusal raised after a match keeps that match's klass OMP-403-s06: a non-research identity whose request a standing network_access destination would allow is still refused klass standing: git-receive-pack on any host (query service=git-receive-pack or a path ending /git-receive-pack, including after percent-decoding) with code git_receive_pack, and a non-GET/HEAD, tunneled, or bodied request to a project remote host with code control_plane_action; both keep the standing policy id. GET/HEAD without a body to that host, and a non-receive-pack request to a standing host that is not a project remote, stay allowed standing. Research returns before this rule.

OMP-431-s08-s02 research filesystem jail, started as unshare --mount --pid --fork python -m omp_work.egress_research_jail. A research root reads ca_cert_path before any mount and exits nonzero without writing a certificate when the path is missing, unreadable, or empty. Makes / rprivate, mounts a tmpfs as the new root, read-only rbinds /usr, and recreates /bin, /lib, /lib64, and /sbin as the host symlink or a read-only rbind. Writes /etc/passwd and /etc/group from the host, the shared s06 resolver texts, and the CA bytes at /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt. Bind-mounts /dev/null, /dev/zero, /dev/random, and /dev/urandom. Mounts a fresh procfs, or on EPERM or EACCES leaves /proc empty and never bind-mounts the host /proc. /tmp is mode 1777 and a research root creates /home/research. pivot_root(new, new/.old), chdir /home/research for a research root, creates setup_ok through the old root, umount2 /.old with MNT_DETACH, removes /.old, and execve's setpriv --bounding-set=-all --inh-caps=-all --no-new-privs plus the config argv with the research worker environment. Does not call chroot. Imports happen at module load, before the pivot. Codacy: the jail root, /home, and /home/research chmod 0755 and /tmp chmod 1777 are the intended POSIX modes for a tmpfs root the unprivileged worker must traverse, and the setpriv execve is a fixed argv list with no shell and no user-controlled executable, so the Bandit B103/B606 and insecure-file-permissions/dangerous-os-exec findings are suppressed with nosec/nosemgrep. OMP-417: root "worker" returns before the CA read. It builds the same tmpfs jail without a CA file and without /home/research, bind-mounts the config worktree read-write at /work, and bind-mounts each absolute ro_binds file read-only at the caller's path. The read-only remount keeps the source mount's nosuid, nodev, noexec, nosymfollow, atime, and relatime flags so a user namespace accepts it. pivot_root then chdirs to /work. The research root still requires the CA, still creates /home/research, and still chdirs there.

OMP-431-s06/s07: egress sandbox runner. Executes the worker in isolated user, mount, network, and PID namespaces with an AF_UNIX record.sock (mode 0700) listener that records refused raw egress attempts as EgressRecord entries on channel raw with code raw_egress_refused; unshare, setpriv, and ip must be on PATH and run by absolute path, the worker command is the caller argv with no shell, and a recorder failure is ignored. run_sandboxed also takes gateway=None, workservice (host, port)|None, and ca_cert_path=None: with a gateway it calls gateway.open_sandbox(identity, dir) (closing it afterward) and binds <dir>/dns.sock (chmod 0600), answering A/AAAA from the gateway resolver only for the model proxy host, a named registry or remote host, or an unexpired standing host the gateway policy_source(identity, now) grants, refusing every other name with code name_not_allowed recorded on channel dns and never forwarding it; with workservice it binds <dir>/ws.sock (chmod 0600), a relay that connects only to that host and port; without a gateway or workservice neither socket exists and names fail as before. OMP-431-s08-s01: run_sandboxed raises ResearchStageRefused('research_stage_launcher') for a research-stage identity before any tool lookup or process, and run_research_stage(argv, identity, <run_sandboxed args>, cwd=None, context_paths=()) refuses before any process with ResearchStageRefused('worktree_not_allowed') for a non-None workdir or cwd, 'context_not_allowed' for non-empty context_paths, and 'credential_not_allowed' for an env key that is not PATH, LANG, TERM, TZ, or LC_* (case-insensitive), then runs the same body through one private runner with config root "research" (run_sandboxed passes None) and workdir None. OMP-417: run_sandboxed and the shared body also take root, ro_binds, and worktree. worktree is written into config.json only when set and ro_binds only when non-empty, so a research config is unchanged. root "worker" selects the worktree jail. A research-stage identity is still refused before any process.

OMP-431-s06/s07: sandbox setup helper: brings up lo and dummy egress0 with default routes, taps egress0 via AF_PACKET to record TCP SYN and UDP flows, bind-mounts isolated /etc/ files, masks sockets and helper cmdline, and executes worker via unshare. ip, mount, unshare, setpriv, true, and gcc are executed by absolute path; worker unshare is resolved on the worker PATH so a mount-proc shim directory prepended to PATH still wins. The worker argv is the caller command as a list with no shell. A failed tap datagram or socket/cmdline mask is ignored and setup continues. OMP-431-s07: when the runner bound a gateway or WorkService relay, the helper masks sibling sandboxes by mounting a tmpfs over the socket root and binding only this sandbox's directory back (so record.sock stays reachable; the directory is held open as /proc/self/fd/N and mount(2) is called directly so the source is not canonicalized), then exposes UDP 127.0.0.1:53 to the gateway dns.sock (the AF_UNIX reply is sent to a dns.client.sock the helper binds), TCP 127.0.0.1:3128 to the gateway proxy.sock, and TCP 127.0.0.1:<workservice port> to ws.sock; the worker env (not the helper's) gets HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, ALL_PROXY and their lowercase forms = http://127.0.0.1:3128, an empty NO_PROXY/no_proxy, and SSL_CERT_FILE, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, GIT_SSL_CAINFO set to ca_cert_path; Codacy: the worker Popen is an argv list with no shell and an env the caller supplied, so the tainted-env Semgrep rule is suppressed with nosemgrep; OMP-431-s08-s02: a root of research skips the mount-proc shim and does not touch setup_ok; after the same network, tap, resolver-file, socket-mask, and relay setup, the helper runs unshare --mount --pid --fork on python -m omp_work.egress_research_jail with the config path. The research worker environment copies only PATH, LANG, TERM, TZ, and LC_* from the config env (PATH defaults to /usr/bin:/bin), sets HOME to /home/research, adds the s07 proxy variables when proxy_sock is set, and sets SSL_CERT_FILE, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, and GIT_SSL_CAINFO to the in-jail certificate /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt. resolv.conf, nsswitch.conf, and hosts texts are module constants shared with the jail. A null root is unchanged. OMP-417: root "worker" is accepted with research: it skips the mount-proc shim, does not touch setup_ok, and runs the same jail unshare. The worker environment copies only PATH, LANG, TERM, TZ, OMP_TASK_TOKEN, and OMP_WORK_URL from the config env (PATH defaults to /usr/bin:/bin) and does not set HOME, proxy, CA, or LC_*. Any other named root still exits 125 before setup_ok exists.

OMP-431-s02: EgressStoreMixin in the PostgresWorkStore bases (egress_store.py) owning project_egress_policies and egress_records; put_project_egress inserts a new owner-signed egress version when egress_change_kind (create/widen/narrow against the active row) is authorized by authorize_standing_change, clearing active on the row it replaces and refusing with ProjectAuthorityRefused(code) and no write otherwise; a remote that is not a project repository URL is refused unknown_remote and a registry that is not a bare https origin is refused invalid_registry; load_egress_policy compiles the active egress row and the active network_access standing policies through build_policy (nothing in the project's checkout contributes); record_egress appends one EgressRecord row (mission_id carries no foreign key); list_egress_records reads them for the project or one mission; StoreEgressRecorder(store, workspace_id, actor_id) writes each verdict through record_egress

OMP-431-s05 GatewayCA for TLS-inspected tunnels, shelling out to openssl with a fixed argv (no new dependency, the v1/owner_signature.py style). __init__(state_dir) raises TlsUnavailable when openssl is not on PATH, creates state_dir 0700, and creates a CA once: an EC P-256 self-signed ca.crt with basicConstraints CA:TRUE and keyUsage keyCertSign,cRLSign, writing ca.key 0600 and ca.crt 0644; an existing ca key and cert are reused. ca_cert_path is the ca.crt path and is the only file a sandbox is given; the key never leaves. leaf_context(host) returns a cached server SSLContext for a leaf signed by the CA with subjectAltName DNS:<host> or IP:<host>, minted on first use under leaves/<safe host>/ from an EC key (0600), a CSR, an openssl x509 CAcreateserial signature, and an ext file that sets basicConstraints CA:FALSE, keyUsage digitalSignature,keyEncipherment, and extendedKeyUsage serverAuth. An openssl call that exits non-zero or times out raises TlsUnavailable with its stderr; a client trusting only ca_cert_path verifies the leaf, and a leaf the CA did not sign fails verification; Codacy: the state-dir chmod 0o700 (owner-only, the execute bit makes it traversable) is the Semgrep insecure-file-permissions false positive suppressed with nosemgrep.

OMP-415-s06: load_allowed_hosts(config_dir) returns a lower-cased frozenset of push-destinations.json allowed_hosts, or an empty frozenset when the file is missing or not that shape. check_destination(url, *, allowed_hosts, resolve=getaddrinfo IPs) returns scheme for a non-https URL, userinfo when the URL carries credentials, host_not_allowed when the host is outside the allowlist, unresolvable when resolve fails or returns no addresses, blocked:<reason> when egress_policy.blocked_address refuses any resolved IP, and None when every resolved IP is allowed. OMP-415-s07: body_bytes is sorted compact JSON; signature is v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256(key, idem + "\n" + body)> and verify compares that header as ASCII bytes, returning False for a missing, non-ASCII, or non-matching header without raising; subscription_key derives a per-subscription key as HMAC-SHA256(master, "omp-push-subscription\0" + sub_id); load_master_key reads push-signing.key and raises ValueError when it is missing, shorter than 32 bytes, or group/other readable (mode & 0o077); send_signed POSTs the canonical body bearer-less with X-OMP-Signature through grokbot.send, which does not follow redirects (a 3xx is a GrokbotError), retrying GrokbotError after sleep(1) then sleep(2) and raising the third. run_push walks every client's subscriptions, skips rows with no push_url and ops.* streams other than event_types exactly ["ops.alarm"], refuses an unsafe push_url with {"refused": reason} before sending, delivers each subscribed mission event once with Idempotency-Key = mission_event_id, advances the cursor to next_after_sequence with operation_id = uuid5(NAMESPACE_URL, f"omp-push-cursor:{id}:{seq}"), and on a send failure advances only to the last delivered event and returns {"failed": reason}. OMP-415-s08-s02: an event_types == ["ops.alarm"] row is served instead of skipped — _replay_ops pages client.events(after_sequence, limit=500) from 0 until has_more is false or a page is empty, feeding each page to alarm_classify.classify with one fresh AlarmState carried across pages and returning (alerts, rest, events); _push_ops_alarm sends each alert whose sequence is past the cursor, in order, with Idempotency-Key alert.idempotency_key and body alert.body(), advances the cursor to the last scanned event sequence when past the cursor after all are sent, and on a send exception advances to the failed alert's sequence minus one when past the cursor then returns {"failed": reason} OMP-415-s08-s03: run_push gains keyword today: date | None = None, and None means datetime.now(timezone.utc).date(). An event_types == ["ops.digest"] row is served on its own cursor with the same push_url refusal, per-subscription key, send, and _advance handling as ops.alarm. From _replay_ops (alerts, rest, events), events are grouped by alarm_classify._to_utc_date(occurred_at); a day's last sequence is the max event sequence that day. For each day d < today, ascending, whose last sequence is past the cursor, the body is build_digest(workspace_id, d, rest, n) where n is the count of alerts whose occurred_at UTC date is d, sent with Idempotency-Key digest:{workspace_id}:{d.isoformat()}; pushed increments by 1 and the cursor advances to d's last sequence, which is the cursor for the next day. A send exception returns {"failed": str(error)} and does not advance the cursor.

Public native research jobs API (R03, OMP-324, OMP-400) on the shared omp_jobs substrate: store, enqueue/claim admission, worker register/drain, trial projection, settled-trial bind diagnostic, usage recording, lease reconciliation/renewal/settlement, outbox delivery, and worker runtime (JobWorker, Handler, Settlement, load_handler). No WorkService command or read surface change

enqueue_job and claim_job run through NativeJobStore.run_operation. Enqueue requires resources cpu/memory_mib/gpu/model_calls as integers >= 0, capabilities stored sorted and unique, lease_seconds 1..3600, a work item and parent in the workspace, and, when trial_id is set, a proposed trial of that work on an admitted or running campaign. A cancelled parent or ancestor raises job_cancelled and writes no row. An identical job_id replays; any other row with that id is idempotency_conflict. The insert is source native, backlog, fence 0, plus an enqueued event. OMP-404-s05 adds an item-budget gate after the validations and before the insert, for the root item (the parent's chain top, or the work item itself): an exhausted usd/tokens/wall_clock dimension cancels the item tree and refuses, and a child that would take the tree past max_subagents cancels the tree and writes the subagents budget.exceeded alert first. A refusal returns {status refused, code budget_exceeded} from apply, and because a raise inside the transaction would roll back the alert and the stop, enqueue_job raises JobError budget_exceeded only after the transaction commits (replays included). After a child insert the same transaction calls check_item_budget, so a child that crosses a subagents threshold writes the 50 or 80 row at enqueue. claim_job reads only the workers row, locks it, and with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED considers the oldest backlog native job whose capabilities the worker holds, whose resource weight (sum of the four fields) fits capacity minus the weight of that worker's unreleased reservations, that fits caller-specified resource_limits (cpu/memory_mib/gpu/model_calls >= 0) against unreleased reservations plus the candidate job, and that has no cancelled ancestor; a candidate whose root item budget is exhausted returns job null instead of being leased. A trial job is leased only while the trial is proposed, the campaign is admitted or running, and the worker component is in compatibility.workers. The lease sets admitted, fence+1, attempt+1, worker_id, lease_expires_at, reservation {job_id}:{fence}, and a claimed event. An unknown or inactive worker is job_worker_unavailable; no match returns job null. OMP-430-s06: claim_job, as the first statement inside its transaction and before it locks the worker row, returns {status applied, job null} when the workspace's agent stop is engaged, so no job is leased (and no fence is spent) while stopped; the owner's release lets the next claim resume the same backlog job OMP-417-s05: after the worker is confirmed active and before the backlog scan, claim_job returns the oldest admitted job already leased to that worker which has a lease_resumed event not yet followed by a later resume_claimed; it appends resume_claimed with payload worker_id and fence and does not change the worker, fence, or reservation. An unknown or inactive worker still raises job_worker_unavailable before that lookup, and a stop still returns job null before the worker is locked.

OMP-404: item budget accounting, threshold alerts, and the budget-driven stop. item_budget reads the payload.draft.budget of the work item's newest intake_publication receipt (None when the receipt or its budget is absent). root_work_id walks the parent_job_id chain to its top work item, bounded against a self-parent cycle. item_spend sums price_usd and input+output tokens over the recursive CTE of the work item's jobs plus every parent_job_id descendant whichever work item it belongs to, plus the work item's job-less usage, and reports wall_clock_seconds as the age of the oldest tree job and subagents as the count of tree jobs with a parent. check_item_budget is a no-op for an unbudgeted item; otherwise it writes one committed budget_alert outbox row per reached threshold, keyed by sha256(workspace, work, dimension, threshold) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, carrying event budget.threshold_reached at 50 and 80 and budget.exceeded at 100, dimension, threshold_percent, spent, and limit, and (OMP-430-s05) the work_id. usd, tokens, and wall_clock_seconds alert at 50/80/100 and report the dimension exhausted once spend reaches the limit; subagents alerts at 50/80 by count/max only (silent when max is 0) and is never exhausted. OMP-404-s05: when any dimension is exhausted, check_item_budget also calls cancel_item_tree with reason budget_exceeded in the same transaction, so the alerts and the item-tree stopping commit together. sweep_item_budgets visits the workspace's source=native work items that carry an intake_publication receipt and have a non-terminal job, each in its own transaction, and returns the work ids whose tree check_item_budget stopped (work-clock enforcement with no usage row). alert_subagents_exceeded writes the subagents budget.exceeded row at the cap; the enqueue refusal path calls it, since check_item_budget never reports subagents exhausted

OMP-430-s05: relay_budget_alerts(job_store, work_store, *, workspace_id, actor_id) reads the workspace's committed or failed kind='budget_alert' outbox rows in event_id order under FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, commits a failed row again first, and for each row executes one work_store.execute(record_alarm_signal, actor_id, actor_kind='automation', required_scope='work.mutate') with signal budget_exceeded for payload event budget.exceeded else cost_threshold, the payload work_id, subject "<dimension> budget <threshold_percent>% reached", detail "spent <spent> of <limit>", and operation/request/correlation ids uuid5(NAMESPACE_URL, "omp-work:budget-alert:" + event_id); success acknowledges and closes the row, a store error returns it to failed (ack_token NULL) for retry under that same deterministic operation id, and a payload that is not a JSON object fails the row without recording, matching jobs/grokbot's earlier read/lock/closeout. Returns the count of rows relayed

cancel_job runs through NativeJobStore.run_operation. It locks the target and every same-workspace descendant with a recursive CTE on parent_job_id, FOR UPDATE, ordered by job_id. Each native backlog or admitted job becomes cancelled with cancel_reason, cancelled_at, and updated_at; an admitted job also gains fence+1, loses worker_id, and has its open {job_id}:{fence} reservation released as cancelled, so the holder's renew and settle raise job_fence_stale. Sealed and failed jobs stay. One cancelled event is appended per job cancelled. The result is {status, job_ids}. A target already cancelled for the same reason replays and does not write the job, its events, or its reservation again; a different reason is idempotency_conflict. A missing target, or a sealed or failed target, is invalid_request and writes nothing. OMP-404-s05 adds cancel_item_tree, the item-scoped counterpart the budget stopper calls with the caller's open cursor: it validates the reason, locks the work item's own jobs plus every parent_job_id descendant (whichever work item), in job_id order FOR UPDATE, then cancels the native backlog and admitted rows through the same _cancel_rows rules. It is a sub-operation of the enclosing transaction, not run_operation, so it stamps the enclosing operation id and has no separate replay; sealed, failed, and already-cancelled jobs are left alone

renew_lease, settle_job, and reconcile_jobs run through NativeJobStore.run_operation. Renew and settle hold only a native admitted job whose worker_id and fence match and whose lease_expires_at is still after now; otherwise job_fence_stale and nothing is written. renew_lease adds lease_seconds to the job lease and the unreleased {job_id}:{fence} reservation expiry. settle_job maps succeeded to sealed and failed to failed. Each receipt role is audit, release, or evaluator; its evidence must validate as an R02 evidence document of kind receipt, and its issuer must be a registered workspace component whose kind equals that role; otherwise invalid_request and nothing is written. Settlement {outcome, fence, worker_id, receipts} is written once with settled_at, the reservation is released as settled, and a settled event is appended. A terminal job replays a byte-identical settlement under a new operation id and keeps the stored receipts; any other settlement is job_fence_stale. With no stop to apply, reconcile_jobs returns each admitted native job with lease_expires_at at or before now to backlog with fence+1, null worker_id and lease_expires_at, releases that reservation as lease_expired, appends a lease_expired event, and returns {status, job_ids}; a second call returns no job ids.
